name: Rodeo Drive / Special Events / Holiday Program Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday
  Program Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Thursday, January 18, 2024
  4:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 18, 2024 / 4:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Lily Bossie, Deputy City
  Manager Kieth Sterling, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis,
  Special Events Film Coordinator Patricia Betancourt, Police Sergeant Paul
  Kim, Parking Services Manager Genevieve Row, Public Information
  Manager Lauren Santillana

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Members of the public were given the opportunity to directly address the
  Committee on any item not listed on the agenda.
  b. Farhang Foundation Director Alireza Ardekani
  i. He expressed his thanks to the Council for partnering with the Farhang
  Foundation and is looking forward to Nowruz 2024.
  c. Steve Meyer
  i. He stated that the agenda and agenda report for this meeting was not
  available three days prior to the meeting and expressed his wish for Vice
  Mayor Friedman to focus on transparency when he becomes Mayor.
  ii. Vanity Fair:
  1. Have Public Works provide a sign a week in advance of the closure
  of the line 617 bus stop at the corner of Crescent and Santa Monica
  showing where the stop will be relocated to during the closure.
  2. Relocate the line 4 bus stop from in front of City Hall to the
  southwest corner of Santa Monica and Rexford like what occurred
  during 2023 instead of closing the stop.
  3. Disallow street parking for Vanity Fair tractor trailers in the industrial
  area on Maple Drive, 3rd Street, Foothill Drive, and/or Civic Center
  Drive.
  iii. LA Marathon
  1. Have Public Works post 3’ x 6’ signs two weeks in advance of the
  marathon stating that Doheny will be closed for the marathon. Signs
  should be posted on the eastbound side of 3rd Street, Alden Drive,
  Beverly Boulevard, Civic Center Drive, and Santa Monica
  Boulevard.
  d. Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce
  i. The chamber expresses their support for the LA Marathon and its proposed
  route through the city.

  ii. They encourage the marathon to work to minimize disruption to traffic and
  businesses considering Metro construction on Wilshire, and to follow
  proper safety protocols for all participants and attendees.
  e. In response to Mr. Meyer’s comments about the unavailability of the agenda and
  agenda report, the City’s Community Outreach Manager stated that the agenda
  was posted on the Friday prior to the meeting and suspects that it was either a
  browser or computer issue that prevented him from seeing the agenda.

  2) Request to Consider the Placement of Persian New Year (Nowruz) Street Pole
  Banners in Beverly Hills for 2024:
  a. Report by Magdalena Davis
  i. The city has traditionally partnered with the Farhang Foundation for the
  display of Nowruz banners across the city.
  ii. 2023 saw an expansion of banner locations in addition to a new design for
  the banners.
  iii. Banner placement will be from March 1st to April 1st.
  iv. Banner locations will be at: Wilshire Blvd, La Cienega, South Santa Monica,
  North Canon, North Beverly, and a street span banner across the
  intersection of Santa Monica and Wilshire.
  v. 89 total banners.
  vi. Estimated cost of $9,182.33 for cleaning, day overlays, installation, and
  removal, which is already budgeted for.
  vii. Will go to the full council for approval on February 6th.
  b. The number of banners increased from 32 to 89 in 2023 and were only displayed
  in the Business Triangle.
  c. Only area not covered by this campaign that has been covered by other campaigns
  is Olympic, which would require an additional 6 to 8 banners to cover.
  d. New banners are $170 each, meaning an additional 8 banners would cost $1360.
  e. The typical lifespan of a banner is between 3-5 years.
  f. The $170 per banner is from a set contract with A3, who makes the banners for
  the city.
  g. Installation costs would not increase for the 8 additional banners.
  h. Both members of the council have directed staff to include Olympic in the areas
  where banners are displayed, which would increase the total cost to approximately
  $10,542.

  3) Informational Update from Vanity Fair for Post-Academy Awards Event on Sunday,
  March 10,2024, including closure of 400 Block of North Crescent Drive, as Part of
  Three-Year Agreement (2022-2024):
  a. Closure would be for the Vanity Fair Academy Awards dinner and Post Party,
  which the city has hosted for the past ten years.
  b. Attendance is expected to be in the thousands.
  c. Vanity fair will partner with local chef Evan Funke to provide dinner for the event.
  d. Officers will be on full deployment the day of the event while traffic control
  personnel will monitor all traffic activity in the area.
  e. Lane and sidewalk closures on 400 N Crescent will begin on February 26th, while
  surrounding closures and extended lane closures will begin on March 10th. The
 Highlights for January 18, 2024
Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  extended lane closures will reopen by 4:00 AM and 400 N Crescent will reopen
  March 14th.
  f. Notifications will be sent out to all business and residents affected by the closures.
  In addition to these notifications, the city will also send out Nixle alerts, social media
  announcements, and post advertisements in the local paper to inform residents of
  the closure.
  g. The city will also man a hotline number during the event to deal with questions
  from residents.
  h. All expenses related to the closure are the responsibility of Vanity Fair and will be
  paid in full prior to the event date.
  i. Liaison feedback is requested for the street and sidewalk closures and the closure
  flat rate fee. If approved, it will go to the full council on February 6th.
  j. Crescent closures have been modified so that the crosswalks are still usable.
  k. Due to the 400 Crescent Street closures, the Crecent City Hall voting center will
  be closed. Early voting will instead be held at the City Library auditorium, and at
  Roxbury and La Cienega parks. The same number of voting machines will be used.
  l. Rexford parking meters will be blocked off in front of the library and several
  Rexford parking structure spots will be allocated to library voters to facilitate voting
  access.
  m. Voters will have access to the vote center regardless of library hours.
  n. The City Clerk’s office is working with the City’s communication office to inform the
  public about the new voting location.
  o. Information about the street closures is ready to be released to the public following
  the council approval on February 6th.
  p. Non social media outreach will begin with a press release immediately following
  council approval.
  q. Vanity Fair will be booking Steak 48 for an event.
  r. The contractors for the construction at the event will be working closely with the
  fire department and building and safety inspectors.

  4) Request from Allen Media Group for Special Event held at The Beverly Wilshire
  Hotel including Alleyway Closure on Sunday, March 10, 2024:

  The Allen Group cancelled this event, so the item was struck from the agenda.

  5) Informational Update from Los Angeles Marathon for Special Events Street
  Closures on Sunday, March 17, 2024, as part of Three-Year Agreement (2023-2025):
  a. Presentation by Patricia Betancourt
  i. The Beverly Hills segment of the Marathon will go down from Doheny onto
  Burton Way, past City Hall onto South Santa Monica, down Rodeo to
  Wilshire, before proceeding to North Santa Monica Boulevard.
  ii. LA Marathon averages over 25,000 participants.
  iii. Road closures will be along the route listed in I from 5 AM to 1 PM.
 Highlights for January 18, 2024
Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  iv. Beverly Hills PD and Public Works personnel will be present at key
  intersections to assist with traffic management and safety.
  v. Notifications will be sent out to all business and residents affected by the
  closures. In addition to these notifications, the city will also send out Nixle
  alerts, social media announcements, and post advertisements in the local
  paper to inform residents of the closure.
  vi. The city will also man a hotline number during the event to deal with
  questions from residents.
  vii. All expenses for this event are the responsibility of the McCourt Foundation
  and will be paid prior to the event. The McCourt Foundation will receive the
  non-profit rate for street closures.
  b. Reopening’s are rolling across the city, with Doheny reopening around 12:00 PM
  and additional reopening’s coming later until the last reopening around 1:00 PM.
  c. Mr. Meyer’s suggestions will be taken under advisement.
  d. All traffic control officers will have cards to hand out to drivers regarding traffic
  closures and detours.

  6) 2023 Citywide Holiday Décor Feedback and Information:
  a. Lights on Wilshire need restringing,
  b. Blue lights do not need programmable RGB as the blue is the only color used.
  c. The orbs on Wilshire also need replacement.
  d. Feedback about South Beverly décor has described it as repetitive and lacking the
  elegance of the other areas.
  e. Staff is requesting to replace the décor for South Beverly, La Cienega, and South
  Santa Monica.
  f. Request to install artificial grass at Beverly Gardens under the tree due to the foot
  traffic eroding the natural grass to mud.

  7) Future Agenda Items:

  None

  8) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: January 18, 2024 / 5:30 PM
